editorial:
Imagine taking a trip to the middle of nowhere to fix your marriage, only to find out your husband is turning into a monster. You follow Blake and Charlotte as they head to a creepy old farmhouse in Oregon. The vibe is super tense from the start. You feel the panic as they get trapped inside while something scary circles the house. It is not just about a monster, though. It is about a couple who are already fighting, which makes the whole situation feel way more stressful and real.

What really works here is how the tension builds up. The acting is great, and the scares hit hard without being too over the top. Some parts might feel a bit slow, but the big payoff at the end makes it worth it. If you love movies that keep you on the edge of your seat, you need to see this. For the best experience, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the dark details. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you find out that the curse is passed down through Blake's family. Charlotte tries to save him, but he completely loses his human side. The twist is that the monster is not just an animal, but a reflection of Blake's inner anger. After a brutal fight in the house, Charlotte manages to survive, but the movie ends with a hint that the creature is still out there in the woods.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves monster movies and psychological thrills.
